newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends sharply higher on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends sharply higher on fund buying.

text.p: A rush of commodity fund buying pushed CBOT soyoil futures to a sharply higher close Monday while soymeal ended mixed, floor traders said.
After a day of somewhat lackluster trading, Rosenthal Collins began buying July soyoil and pushed the market sharply higher during the last twenty minutes of trade, floor sources said.
Rosenthal was said to have purchased up to 1,400 lots of soyoil, pit sources said.
Nearby soymeal futures could not shake off the bearish influnce of old crop soybeans and closed lower.
Soymeal cash markets were quiet Monday, with some dealers reporting end-user buying for spot delivery. Many dealers reported having trouble purchasing soybeans for processing this summer.
The market was also supported by ongoing talk that China is still an active buyer in South American soybean product markets, traders said.
CBOT soyoil ended 0.34 to 0.50 cent per lb higher, with July up 0.36 at 24.14. Soymeal futures ended $1.30 per ton higher to $3.30 per ton lower, with July down $3.30 at $287.20.
In export business, South Korea re-invited tenders for 40,000 tonnes of soymeal, but CBOT traders said the trade was destined for South American exporters.
On the day in soymeal trade, Merrill Lynch sold 500 lots July, ADM sold 300 July and Cargill bought 100 lots July and 100 lots September, pit sources said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 25,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 22,663 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 13,000 lots, against Friday's 22,412 lots.
